verdict.why_winner: C is the only pitch that starts from a gap Ramp's own docs admit (auto-void checks, book to Stale Checks liability, reissue manually), sits directly on Bill Pay data a team can mock faithfully, and produces a tight demo loop with real money movement: detect the voided check, reach the vendor by email or voice, verify ACH against fraud, reissue through Ramp, and fall back to a due-diligence letter and NAUPA file. It fits 'outdated financial workflow' literally (paper checks and unclaimed property), has no competitor inside Ramp, and the 10-day build is realistic. F loses because the core action (filling live state portals) is undemoable and the space is already served.

ideas.label: A
ideas.concern: Demand is speculative. Few small caterers or suppliers will run an x402/MCP endpoint, and buyer agents purchasing from them is still alpha-stage, so the pain is invented ahead of the market even though the PDF-to-endpoint-to-coded-receipt demo would look slick.

ideas.label: B
ideas.concern: The dollar value per company is modest and disputes are infrequent. The live voice call to a merchant could go off-script on stage, so the team needs a reliable scripted or recorded fallback.

ideas.label: C
ideas.concern: Computer use on real state portals (CAPTCHAs, EIN and identity requirements, real fees) can't be shown credibly in 10 days without mocks. Mosey, Gusto and Rippling already handle much of this registration work.

ideas.label: D
ideas.concern: Ramp, Siteline and Procore Pay already cover most of this. The new pieces, chasing waivers and diffing them against statutory text, are thin, and judges outside construction need a primer that eats into demo time.

ideas.label: E
ideas.concern: The workflow is annual and niche, and the most distinctive part (dormancy tracking and NAUPA reports) runs on synthetic multi-year data. The remaining core is essentially an outreach-and-reissue flow.

ideas.label: F
ideas.concern: Customs entries would be fully synthetic, funded startups (Pax, Zollback, Caspian) already do these refunds, and the IEEPA refund wave may be largely processed by the final, so neither the data nor the timing holds up.

verdict.why_winner: B is the most complete agentic loop a student team can build and demo credibly in 10 days. It detects disputable charges from real transaction patterns, pulls evidence from the inbox, escalates to the merchant by email and voice, and produces a dispute packet with the right reason code and a deadline countdown, all behind a human approval gate. Stripe Issuing test mode gives it an end-to-end flow on real infrastructure instead of mocks. It fills an actual gap next to Ramp's existing duplicate-charge flags without duplicating them, the money recovered is concrete, and the voice-call moment would make a memorable demo.

ideas.label: A
ideas.concern: Real state portals can't be hit in a demo, so this becomes computer-use against a student-built fake portal, which proves little; it also sits directly on Ramp for Agents' incorporation roadmap, so it reads as an extension of what we're already building rather than a gap.

ideas.label: B
ideas.concern: Niche and annual, and the multi-year dormancy timeline has to be simulated; the team must keep the live demo on the near-term loop (void detected, vendor contacted, ACH verified, reissued) and not bury the audience in NAUPA formatting.

ideas.label: C
ideas.concern: Forward-looking but the pain is speculative: few companies have agents trying to buy from caterers today, x402 alpha access is uncertain for students, and the demo risks being a crypto-payments toy rather than an outdated-workflow automation.

ideas.label: D
ideas.concern: Overlaps heavily with Ramp's existing duplicate-charge flagging and dispute flow, and the team concedes disputes are rare and small-dollar; the voice-call-the-merchant moment will demo well but the business case is thin.

ideas.label: E
ideas.concern: Everything that matters (customs entries, ACE data, CBP refund flow) is synthetic, funded startups already own this, and the refund wave may be largely processed by demo day, leaving a matching exercise over fake CSVs.

ideas.label: F
ideas.concern: Ramp for Construction already validates waivers and Siteline/Procore already chase them; the statutory-text diff is the only novel piece, and a judge panel will need a lien-waiver primer that eats the 3-5 minutes.

verdict.why_winner: B targets a workflow Ramp explicitly punts to the customer today (void and reissue manually, book to Stale Checks), the pain is concrete and compliance-backed, and the core loop can be built and demoed credibly in 10 days with real Ramp Bill Pay data shapes, email/voice outreach, ACH verification, and a reissue, with the escheatment reporting as a defensible stretch; it is the only pitch that is clearly a gap, clearly demoable, and clearly useful.
